paper.title_en: Static Black Holes and Iyer-Wald Entropy in $f(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{K})$ Gravity
paper.abstract_en: We investigate static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions in a class of {nonpolynomial} gravitational theories described by a {Lagrangian $f=-X^{1-n}$, where $X = \mathcal{R} + \sqrt{6\mathcal{K} - \mathcal{R}^2}$ is a function of the Ricci and Kretschmann scalars.} The modified Einstein equations contain {nonpolynomial} curvature terms. We develop a perturbative scheme to look for a black hole solution that deviates parametrically from the Schwarzschild geometry. We obtain first-order corrections to the metric by solving the resulting coupled differential equations. The corresponding Iyer--Wald entropy is then evaluated consistently to first order in the perturbative coupling. We show that the {nonpolynomial} contribution gives rise to a power-law correction to the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy.
